floor_history.headline: Rotation SOLVED: real do-while outer loop + removing the do-while(0) yoff wrap flips the s2/s3/s4 trio to target's exact allocation; floor 29 -> 22
Named the residual's mechanism from the .loop dump (loop.c LICM hoist breaks combine's symbol-into-MEM fold) and killed it for D_80094DF0 with byte-pointer indexing: floor 22 -> 17 at 135/135 insns.
Floor 17 -> 13: moving `tbl += 2` out of the middle of the loop body removes a REG_DEP_ANTI that stranded the LoadImage arg-setup block, and the inner-loop SCHEDULE is now byte-for-byte target's; the

frontier.hypothesis: Denying hard reg $a1 to the `off` pseudo (129) collapses the entire residual 13 to 0 - every differing insn is downstream of that one allocation, and the instruction stream is otherwise byte-for-byte target's in target's order.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c:1240-1300 calls combine_regs(operand, recog_operand[0]) on the sources of `(set (reg:SI 5 a1) (plus (reg/v:SI 129) (reg:SI 139)))`; combine_regs (local-alloc.c:1884-1896) sees the hard setreg and records $a1 in qty_phys_sugg[qty(129)], and find_free_reg's just_try_suggested pass honours it. $a1 taken forces reload to $t0 for the three loop-hoisted, globally-unallocated invariants 136/137/139, and the y-temp and trailing-constant renames follow. Target has `off` in $v0 = no suggestion, first reg in REG_ALLOC_ORDER.
frontier.next_probe: Two independent, source-visible escapes, both OUTSIDE the loop body (which is the one region s3 could not reach and which is now measured closed): (a) make `off` NOT block-local so reg_qty < 0 and combine_regs bails at local-alloc.c:1826, handing it to global.c - i.e. a form in which `off`'s birth insn sits in a different basic block from its use, e.g. the shift computed in the loop-condition block or under the outer-loop rotation rather than at the top of the body; (b) make $a1 LIVE somewhere inside [born_index, dead_index) so find_free_reg's regs_live_at scan (local-alloc.c:2170) excludes it. Confirm any candidate in ONE build with the instrumented cc1's BB2_SUGG_DEBUG env hook (tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1, prints the `used` and `first_used` hard-reg sets per find_free_reg call) rather than inferring from the score - the hook names the decision directly.

frontier.hypothesis: The trailing `li v1,1 / bne v0,v1` (vs target `li t0,1 / bne v0,t0`) in the `func_8003E2A0() == 1` test is the same global.c allocno-ordering difference as item 1, not an independent divergence.
frontier.mechanism: It is the exact mirror image: ours ALLOCATES the constant 1 to $v1 where target rematerializes it into $t0, while inside the loop ours rematerializes into $t0 where target allocates $v0. One allocno-ordering shift would flip both.
frontier.next_probe: Re-measure only after item 1 lands. If it survives, read .greg's allocno ordering and priorities for the constant-1 pseudo before inventing any lever - do not tune it independently.

frontier.hypothesis: The next modality should be register-allocation-focused rather than structural: the structural axes this function exposes are now measured exhausted.
frontier.mechanism: s2 closed the LICM/combine axis, s3 closed the schedule axis (zero ordering divergence remains), declaration order (15 forms) and inner-body expression shape (33 forms across s2+s3) are both dead. What is left is a single hard-register assignment whose decision procedure is fully named down to the source line.
frontier.next_probe: Drive from the dump, not the score: build once with BB2_SUGG_DEBUG set, read the find_free_reg trace for qty(129), and design the C form against the two documented escape conditions instead of sweeping spellings.
